title: 5 prompts to learn faster

sources.name: Prompting guidance: give context and ask for a specific output

caption:
5 prompts to turn your AI assistant into a study partner: explain, quiz, find gaps, compare and plan reviews.
AI answers can be wrong, so confirm key facts in your course materials or official sources.
Save this study set. Comment LEARN and I will send the prompt list.

slides.headline: Tell it your level
body: Say what you know and what you want to understand.

slides.headline: Explain it simply
body: Use this for any topic that feels too dense.
slides.prompt: Explain [topic] to a complete beginner in plain language. Use one everyday example and define each technical term the first time it appears.

slides.headline: Quiz me
slides.prompt: Ask me five questions about [topic], one at a time. Wait for my answer, tell me if I am right, then explain anything I missed.

slides.headline: Find my gaps
body: Paste your own summary and let it spot what is missing.
slides.prompt: Here is my summary of [topic]: [summary]. List what is missing, unclear or possibly wrong, so I can check my sources.

slides.headline: Compare two ideas
body: Side-by-side tables make differences easy to see.
slides.prompt: Compare [concept A] and [concept B] in a table: what each is, how they differ and when each applies.

slides.headline: Build a review plan
body: Fit it to the days you actually have.
slides.prompt: Make a review schedule for [topic] over [number] days, with short daily sessions and one practice test on the last day.

slides.headline: Check it against real sources
body: AI can sound sure and still be wrong.
Confirm key facts in your textbook or official sources.

slides.headline: Short sessions are easier to keep
body: Regular practice beats one long cram.

slides.headline: Save this study set
body: Comment LEARN and I will send the prompt list.
Share this with a friend who is studying.
